revisions.value: Conformance checks are declared in one registry

The check surface accreted piece-by-piece into four shapes for one goal (check-*.mjs assertions, gen-*.mjs --check byte-closure gates, migrate-*.mjs --check applied-gates, tests/*/run.mjs suites) plus an invisible fifth tier of checks deliberately outside validate-all (check-release-drift, which needs the pinned binary). The cost stopped being theoretical on 2026-08-26: train unit #483's agent ran validate-all, got exit 0, and shipped PR #493 red because the drift gate lives outside the surface it checked - nothing declared that the surface had a second half. In grid terms the checks are sound Conformance machinery, but the registry of checks was undeclared structure, inferred by reading a 260-line script - an Earth violation (structure is declared, never inferred) and a meta-level one-way-per-goal failure.

Cell: Conformance. Every spec-repo conformance check is declared in a single registry (scripts/checks.json) rather than hand-wired: each entry names the check's id, script, arguments, tier (always | pinned-cli | ci-only), the grid cell it guards, the governing decision or RFC that introduced it, and an optional expiry for checks born of grandfathering. validate-all.mjs becomes a loop over the registry filtered by tier, and it ends every run by naming the checks deferred to other tiers, so its exit 0 can never again be mistaken for the full gate surface. A membership guard enforces the registry: a check script present on disk but absent from the registry fails the build, which makes piecemeal addition structurally impossible. New checks follow one naming convention; existing script names migrate only when next touched (rename is a migration). The registry is a stepping stone, not the destination: the end state is the checks described as records - the spec repository declaring its own conformance gates the way it declares everything else, with the JSON registry generated as a projection. Owner, 2026-08-26: as long as we keep working towards the goal where all meaning is in SRS we are going in the right direction.

Binds how conformance checks are added to the srs spec repository from ratification: declaration in the registry precedes wiring, the membership guard enforces it, and the tier vocabulary is the one named here. Does not force-rename existing scripts, does not bind sibling repositories (their gates follow their own contracts), and does not build the checks-as-records fold now - that lands with the SRS-for-Specs work and the #490 meaning-placement pass, which this record hands the fold to.

(1) Status quo hand-wiring - rejected by evidence: it produced four conventions and today's red PR. (2) Jumping straight to checks-as-records - deferred, not rejected: it is the declared end state, but building it now widens the current phase; the registry file is the smallest declaration that makes the later fold trivial. (3) Adopting a test-framework dependency to organise the checks - rejected: the problem is undeclared structure, not missing machinery; the fix is data, not a framework.

One added indirection between validate-all and the scripts. The ci-only tier can declare a check but cannot enforce that the CI workflow actually runs it - the registry makes the gap visible in review rather than closing it. Registry entries carry provenance fields that must be filled honestly at addition time.

revisions.value: Fold the registry into records and generate the JSON as a projection when SRS-for-Specs authoring (srs#214 / the #490 pass) makes records the natural home. Review earlier if a second gate is ever discovered outside the declared surface - that would mean the tier vocabulary or the membership guard is incomplete.
